Adding a residual where there was no edge gives a large gain, while replacing an existing conv or pool with skip changes little.
If node 1 does not feed the output directly, cutting its input loses less, so the edit is less harmful.
If node 1 does not feed node 2, it has fewer downstream uses, so removing edge 0 hurts less.
When edge 0 is none, node 1 is all zeros, so a conv on edge 2 adds no useful computation.
When edge 0 is none, node 1 carries no signal, so a conv from node 1 to the output cannot help.
Turning an absent edge into a conv adds depth and capacity, a bigger gain than swapping out an existing op.
Adding a conv where edge 1 was absent enriches node 2's input more than replacing skip or pool does.
Without the input->output edge, removing edge 5 leaves only edge 4 to reach the output, which severely limits the cell.
